PullRequest.Title: Allow remote chats to refresh sandbox CA status without host control
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.

-->

## Problem

A remote chat could show “Sandbox trusted CA is not installed (optional)” with no way to recheck after the user trusted the CA using the CLI. Both capability advertisement and RPC dispatch treated Refresh as a host-management operation, even though it only rechecks certificate status. The notice also did not tell users which CLI commands to run.

## Fix

Allow supported direct connections to advertise and execute the read-only CA refresh when host-control methods are disabled. Preserve relay restrictions, chat and runtime-scope validation, and the existing gates on installing, rotating, and removing trust. Keep the remote notice compact: show the current product’s `agent sandbox ca create` and `agent sandbox ca trust` commands inline, with **Learn more** last. The existing **Refresh** button rechecks the host; it does not change OS trust.

Follow-up to #345281.

## Validation

- `node test\unit\node\index.js --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/protocolServerHandler.test.ts --grep 'sandbox certificate'` — 11 passed, including direct refresh with management disabled, relay rejection, and rejection of trust-changing operations.
- `node test\unit\browser\index.js --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions/agentHostSandboxNotification.test.ts --browser chromium --reporter dot` — 152 passed, 15 pending, 0 failed.
- Rendered the Stable and Insiders banners with the real chat notification widget and verified the product-specific commands, final link, and Refresh button. Live OS trust changes were not exercised.

To verify end to end, connect a remote chat to an updated direct host with refresh support and missing CA trust. As the agent host’s OS user, run the two commands shown in the notice, then select **Refresh**. Once the host reports the CA as trusted, the notice should clear without reconnecting.

Scenarios.Scenario: A direct remote client initializes against an agent host with host-control extension methods disabled.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Protocol initialization constructs and returns capability metadata; the added refresh capability is a constant boolean property and does not perform certificate work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Agent-host protocol initialize request and response.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing protocol exchange per connection; the diff only adds one metadata property to eligible responses.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same initialization exchange occurred without advertising the refresh capability when allowExtensionMethods was false.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Initialization already waits for the response, but the added property contributes only constant serialization work.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of direct client connections; added work is constant per connection.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One initialization response per connection; no new queue, limiter, or fan-out is involved.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache lookup or invalidation is added; capability support is read from the in-memory service and transport state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the complete initialization hunk and response construction were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of simultaneous connections varies, but the per-connection metadata delta is negligible.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; the diff adds only constant-size capability metadata on this path.

Scenarios.Scenario: A focused remote chat with a missing sandbox CA renders its certificate notification.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Subscription/focus/visibility changes call _updateCertificate; when the existing state guard permits rendering, the notification creates a Markdown description and updates the focused chat input notification.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One visible notification for the focused chat; the diff adds two short command strings and two inline code nodes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous UI update for one focused chat; the existing state equality guard suppresses unchanged rerenders.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing in-memory state comparison avoids rebuilding an unchanged notification. IProductService is an injected in-memory product descriptor, not a boundary read.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: constructor ownership, focus guards, equality suppression, and notification construction were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact DOM rendering cost is not measured, but cardinality and payload are tightly bounded.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; the added Markdown and product-name interpolation are bounded and not on a per-row or per-frame loop.

Scenarios.Scenario: A user selects Refresh in a remote direct chat connected to a host with host-control methods disabled.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The click sends one extension request, validates chat/scope on the host, runs the target certificate refresh, then the existing provider implementation waits for diagnostics refresh across live sessions before replying and clearing the UI spinner.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send vscode/refreshSandboxCertificate from the workbench client to the remote agent host and return its result.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per accepted user click; the notification blocks duplicate clicks while one request is active.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: For allowExtensionMethods=false direct hosts, the method gate rejected this request before dispatch and no certificate check ran.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The refresh UI waits for the response.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Query the Copilot SDK certificate proxy for relevance, installation support, and trust status.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: After intentional cache invalidation, up to three sequential SDK RPCs for the clicked configuration, then up to three per distinct uncached runtime credential configuration among live sessions; sessions sharing a key reuse/coalesce the same promise.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This boundary was unreachable through direct clients with host-control disabled; it was already the established refresh behavior for clients where refresh was allowed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The existing refresh implementation awaits these checks before the protocol response; each SDK read is bounded by a five-second timeout.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Distinct live runtime/credential configurations after cache grouping, not raw chat count; one focused user action triggers the scenario.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The UI's _certificateBusy flag coalesces repeated clicks in one notification. Host certificate operations are serialized by SequencerByKey; post-operation live-session diagnostic updates use Promise.all, while the certificate cache coalesces sessions sharing the same runtime credential configuration.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Refresh intentionally invalidates certificate observations. Subsequent diagnostics are cached by runtime and [auth.git, auth.gh, credentials], including failures, and concurrent equivalent reads coalesce. Warm non-refresh diagnostics reuse the cache; each explicit refresh is cold by design.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the full workbench-to-protocol-to-agent-to-SDK call path, cache key, sequencer, Promise.all fan-out, and timeout were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Hosts may have multiple live credential configurations and SDK checks can approach their timeout, but typical cardinality is unknown. The fan-out is pre-existing implementation used by the newly enabled explicit action.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The diff intentionally makes an explicitly requested read-only refresh reachable; duplicate UI clicks are coalesced, SDK checks are bounded and cached by effective configuration, and the changed hunks do not add automatic retries or alter the pre-existing per-refresh fan-out.

Scenarios.Scenario: A relay or passive-relay client initializes or attempts certificate refresh.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Transport/config relay checks suppress capability advertisement or reject dispatch before certificate service execution.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing relay initialize or attempted extension request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One protocol exchange per connection/request; no downstream certificate RPC occurs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Relay refresh was unavailable and remains unavailable.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Relay request handling returns without entering the certificate operation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of relay connections or rejected requests.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No certificate work is scheduled for rejected relay requests.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both capability and dispatch relay gates plus direct/relay tests were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material to the changed behavior.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression; relay restrictions continue to prevent the newly enabled direct-only boundary.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all five changed files and traced initialization, focused-notification rendering, direct refresh dispatch, relay rejection, certificate cache invalidation/coalescing, SDK RPC boundaries, and live-session concurrency. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance regression was found.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
